what_was_done: The code is right, and the single-quote hole is closed and pinned. caller.py now has _QUOTED = r"'[^'\x00-\x1f\x7f]*'". Restoring the old pattern in a scratch copy fails test_allow_list_refuses_every_excluded_character, test_allow_list_regex_refuses_the_tables_on_its_own and test_property_junk_from_excluded_characters_never_approves. A four-shell canary sweep found no text accepted by the allow-list that runs a hidden command. It covered 1851 texts the regex accepts on its own, under sh, bash 3.2, bash 5.3, dash and zsh, run both directly and inside an eval wrapper, with zsh and bash options set. But two rules that ORCH-2 and caller-identity.md state are still not pinned by any test, so a later change could drop them unnoticed. (1) A quoted string holds no character below U+0020 and no U+007F. In a scratch copy, _QUOTED = r"'[^']*'" keeps all 76 tests in test_caller.py, test_shell.py and test_runner.py passing, and so does letting a tab in. The tables test newline and carriage return only in bare text, and the property test's alphabet holds no other control character. (2) A quoted string may follow a bare word only when that word ends with '='. Changing the prefix to (?:(?!=)[SAFE]*)? keeps all 76 tests passing, and no table holds "vsdd survey a'b'". To fix: add "vsdd survey 'a\tb'", "vsdd survey 'a\nb'", "vsdd survey 'a\rb'", "vsdd survey 'a\x00b'", "vsdd survey 'a\x1bb'", "vsdd survey 'a\x7fb'" and "vsdd survey a'b'" to REFUSED_CALLS, so the regex-alone test covers them. Add the other control characters and DEL to the alphabet of the property test's between-quotes position.
